1. HIGH — Turnstile box goes dead after the first refusal. sign-in-parts.tsx:96-103 uses Turnstile's implicit mode (`<script async defer>` plus a `.cf-turnstile` div). That mode draws only the boxes that exist when its script first loads. Proof of the mechanism (scripts/softnav.cjs, at 390 wide with touch): I typed a wrong password on /signin and the answer came back in the SAME document (?problem=wrongEmailOrPassword), with the form element replaced. A marker and a child I had added were both gone. So with Turnstile, the redrawn form has an empty box and sends no answer. It is refused as 'missing', which says "Please try again, with scripts turned on", and every retry does the same until a reload. Even a box that survived would hold an answer siteverify had already spent (timeout-or-duplicate). This is the same for every refusal and for 2.163's redrawn forms. Inferred from Turnstile's documented behaviour, not run against it. Fix: a small client part that loads api.js?render=explicit, calls turnstile.render(el,{sitekey,action,'response-field-name'}) when the form appears and turnstile.remove when it goes. Add a browser test that serves a made-up api.js (page.route for challenges.cloudflare.com, with implicit-on-load behaviour) and checks that a second try after a wrong password carries a fresh answer.
2. MEDIUM — Fails closed, with words that are not true. (a) If the browser cannot load challenges.cloudflare.com (a school or gym network that filters it, or a Cloudflare incident), the form arrives with no answer and the person reads "turn scripts on" (flows.ts botCheckProblem: 'missing' → botCheckFailed). (b) If our server cannot reach siteverify, each try waits up to 10 s (turnstile-bot-check.ts timeout) and then nobody can sign in or sign up. A signed-in scorekeeper keeps working (the proxy renews sessions with no check). A signed-out one at the gym is stuck. Fix now: Turnstile's error-callback writes a fixed word into a hidden field, so the server can say "the check could not load"; cut the timeout to 3–5 s. For the founder (Q2), my recommendation: let 'no-answer' through on T-225's attempt limits alone, with a log line; keep 'key-refused' closed.

All 60 routes are rendered on every request in both builds. Time to first byte, median of 20 runs, two runs each, before → after: home 12.9/11.6 → 15.0/11.6 ms, schedule 12.3/10.9 → 11.1/10.7, team 7.7/7.8 → 8.2/8.2, game 6.9/6.5 → 7.8/7.8. So this step undoes nothing that works today, and the policy can stand. But 2.176's done test, "the build again builds ahead the pages it did before 2.127", is impossible under a nonce policy. A page built ahead has no nonce at all (node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/content-security-policy.md:181 and :391-397: ISR and PPR are incompatible). Its inline self.\_\_next_f scripts would be refused; with the nonce removed, React never ran on any page. Next's own page cache pairs a new nonce from the proxy with old HTML, which also breaks. A shared cache that stores the header together with the body (Cloudflare does) stays consistent. Fix: rewrite 2.176's line and its done test in STAGE-2.md, and record 081's paragraph. Kept pages are kept only by a cache that stores their policy header with them, for a short time; nothing is built ahead.
